one_line: Adaptive web interfaces that let an agent redesign bounded portions of a storefront, dashboard, or data table.
what_it_does: Live Canvas explores bring-your-own-user-interface experiences, with agent-curated layouts and constrained components for shopping, dashboards, and reports.
leverage_rationale: The concept makes structured WebMCP composition central: the agent can reshape a bounded live canvas rather than merely click an existing UI, though the packet does not prove the full workflow end to end.
leverage_evidence: About text describes a bounded WebMCP Live Canvas that the agent redesigns.
Storefront, dashboard, and distribution demos expose structured composition rather than only button actions.
Frame sheets show multiple altered layouts, overlays, and card states.
execution_rationale: The packet shows coherent visual assets and multiple interface states, but no readable end-to-end runtime proof or transcript; execution claims remain only plausibly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Three submitted frame sheets show repeated teal-header UI states, cards, overlays, and forms.
Devpost packaging consistently presents the adaptive-interface concept.
No transcript and no directly verifiable completed workflow.
impact_rationale: Adaptive interfaces could credibly help shoppers researching uncertain purchases and teams needing personalized dashboards or reports.
impact_evidence: About text identifies cart abandonment caused by shoppers needing more information.
Description names storefront, CRM/ERP dashboard, and datatable/report use cases.
Frames show commerce/content-card layouts.
creativity_rationale: Bring-your-own-UI and agent-composed bounded canvases are a memorable, ambitious interaction model beyond ordinary agent automation.
creativity_evidence: The B-Y-O-U-I framing is a distinctive concept.
The project pursues the idea across storefront, dashboard, and component-library scenarios.
Paintbrush/live-canvas visual metaphor is consistently presented.
usability_note: The bounded presets and staged layouts suggest a usable safety-oriented design, but runtime usability is not directly verified.
red_flags: No transcript; frames are small and do not clearly prove live agent invocation.
standouts: Strongly differentiated agent-composed UI concept.
Constrained presets address safety of untrusted web content.
advance_reason: High creativity and meaningful WebMCP leverage justify advancing despite thin runtime evidence.

one_line: A live job-search workspace whose page-registered WebMCP tools let agents search and act while the user approves consequential steps.
what_it_does: JobJam exposes typed tools for job search and application-workspace actions, with credit spending and submissions gated by human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Structured page tools materially improve reliability and safety for a stateful job workflow involving credits and credentials; the agent is central, though a capable general agent could still attempt the UI.
leverage_evidence: Thirteen tools are registered by the page and follow the same path as clicks.
Packet claims approval dialogs owned by the page before spending credits.
Credential isolation and structured filter state are explicit design goals.
execution_rationale: The description is unusually coherent and the development sheets show substantial implementation, but the supplied frames do not clearly show a readable successful search-to-application flow.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported alive.
Frames show substantial code/configuration and multiple states.
About text specifies search, evaluation, rewriting, and approval flows.
impact_rationale: Job seekers have a concrete need for aggregating jobs and preparing applications; approval and credential boundaries address real risks in agent-assisted employment workflows.
impact_evidence: Project is described as a real product with real users, job data, and paid credits.
The workflow targets job search, resume evaluation, rewriting, and cover letters.
Human approval is tied to consequential actions.
creativity_rationale: It is a fresh and well-considered application of WebMCP to a real money-and-credentials job product, though the underlying category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Uses page-native tools as a third path between scraping and hidden API tokens.
Explicitly treats spending and submission approval as product primitives.
The site-is-the-interface framing is coherent.
usability_note: Visible approval boundaries and familiar job-search UI suggest strong usability, subject to runtime verification.
red_flags: Devpost/video thumbnail and small development frames do not prove the advertised end-to-end runtime flow.
standouts: Real product and real credit-spend safety problem.
Clear human-in-the-loop boundary.
advance_reason: Strong leverage, impact, and coherent safety design; advance for direct runtime checking.

one_line: A local-first opportunity workspace for agents to discover, match, and monitor fellowships, internships, and hackathons.
what_it_does: OpportunityOS exposes deterministic browser tools over student-opportunity records, matching and monitoring them with human approval for writes.
leverage_rationale: Deterministic schemas and shared local state are valuable for filtering, matching, and monitoring scattered opportunities, though the same outcomes remain possible with UI automation with friction.
leverage_evidence: Packet claims 11 deterministic tools with strict schemas and human-in-the-loop writes.
Local-first workspace keeps agent and human state together.
Gallery shows dashboard, monitor, progress, and search states.
execution_rationale: The gallery and description support a plausible multi-page workspace, but no frame sheets were submitted and no end-to-end agent result is directly evidenced.
execution_evidence: Seven gallery images show homepage, search, progress, and monitor pages.
Live demo is reported alive and repository is public.
No video frame sheets or transcript were submitted.
impact_rationale: Students and early-career applicants face a real fragmented-opportunity and deadline-tracking problem, and the proposed workspace directly targets it.
impact_evidence: About text identifies fellowships, internships, and hackathons as scattered across sources.
Product targets discovery, matching, and monitoring.
Gallery includes monitoring and progress surfaces.
creativity_rationale: The local-first, agent-native opportunity operating system is a thoughtful synthesis with a clear human approval model, though the category is established.
creativity_evidence: Combines deterministic WebMCP tools with local-first opportunity tracking.
Strict schemas and approval are pursued as core interaction design.
Concept spans search, matching, and monitoring.
usability_note: Multiple focused pages and a local-first model suggest approachable use, but workflow usability is not observed.
red_flags: No submitted frame sheets or video transcript; agent operations are not visibly verified.
standouts: Clear student-oriented problem fit.
Local-first and approval-oriented architecture.
advance_reason: Credible impact and meaningful structured-tool delta, with evidence gap suitable for Stage 2.

one_line: A marketplace where buyer and seller agents negotiate price, quantity, shipping, coupons, and add-ons before human confirmation.
what_it_does: Agent Market exposes storefront and negotiation tools over a large product catalog, runs multi-round deal negotiation, and blocks purchase until the shopper confirms.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables a structured, stateful multi-round negotiation between buyer and seller agents with a human confirmation boundary; general UI-driving is markedly less reliable for this multidimensional deal.
leverage_evidence: About text describes buyer and store agents negotiating over price, quantity, freebie, shipping, and coupons.
Full negotiation tool set is registered on the page.
Confirm dialog prevents purchase until human approval.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent marketplace, tool-agnostic agent loop, pure negotiation state transition, and frame evidence of catalog/detail/transaction states; final negotiation proof is not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported alive.
Frames show product grids, product details, forms, and checkout-like states.
About text specifies one mutation path and economic constraints.
impact_rationale: Shoppers benefit from delegating tedious price and bundle negotiation while retaining control over the purchase; the scenario has clear practical value.
impact_evidence: Product targets real shopping friction beyond simple price lookup.
Multi-dimensional deal terms are explicitly handled.
Frames visibly show a recognizable commerce workflow.
creativity_rationale: Agent-to-agent haggling over a full deal, rather than a single price, is novel and memorable, and the project pursues the interaction deeply.
creativity_evidence: Negotiation covers multiple economic dimensions and rounds.
Buyer and seller agents have distinct roles.
Human confirmation is integrated into the novel flow.
usability_note: Catalog familiarity plus explicit confirmation makes the ambitious negotiation model understandable; runtime details need verification.
red_flags: Frame text is small; final negotiated order approval is not conclusively legible.
standouts: Distinctive multi-dimensional agent negotiation.
Strong economic invariants and human confirmation boundary.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage and creativity with a clear practical commerce use case.

one_line: A browser agent compiles governed WASI deployment intents into verified capsules and produces a bounded portability witness.
what_it_does: UNIV Deploy rejects incompatible releases, verifies digest-bound browser and edge capsules, executes both, and compares declared observations before producing proof.
leverage_rationale: The structured tool surface is central to a consequential multi-step deployment and proof workflow; typed state, bounded artifacts, and verification are impractical to reproduce comparably via generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Five typed WebMCP tools drive compilation, verification, execution, and retrieval.
Packet describes an adversarial incompatible release producing an empty frontier and no capsules.
Receipts and witnesses persist beyond the browser session with integrity checks.
execution_rationale: Description and 99-second transcript provide unusually complete end-to-end evidence: rejection case, permitted compilation, two executions, equality comparison, and durable receipt verification.
execution_evidence: Video transcript explicitly describes two actual WASI executions matching output.
Transcript includes deterministic verifier, digests, receipts, and retrieval rechecks.
Live demo, public repo, and video are reported present.
impact_rationale: Release, platform, and security teams have a concrete need to bound portability claims and avoid granting agents shells or arbitrary code execution.
impact_evidence: About text names platform, release, and security teams as audience.
Product returns a narrower evidence-backed portability claim rather than an unbounded promise.
Transcript demonstrates both success and counterexample handling.
creativity_rationale: The adversarial compile-then-prove portability witness is an ambitious and original interaction model that turns deployment claims into bounded evidence.
creativity_evidence: Starts by challenging the claim with a network-bound counterexample.
Separates target capsules, deterministic verification, execution receipts, and witness generation.
Preserves provenance and distinguishes enforced, observed, pinned, and unattested facts.
usability_note: Strong bounded workflow and visible proof artifacts support expert usability, though deployment concepts are technically demanding.
standouts: Best evidence of a complete consequential workflow.
Adversarial rejection path strengthens trustworthiness.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and execution evidence with a credible high-value developer/security use case.

one_line: A collection manager where agents onboard niche collectibles and provide valuation and monetary analytics under approval.
what_it_does: ShrineKeep stores nested collections and lets an external agent research items, stage edits, and help estimate current value without silently mutating the user's data.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP supplies collection context and safe staged mutations while the agent handles niche research; this is a meaningful improvement over manual entry, but a general agent could achieve much of it with UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text says agent sees the open box and allowed changes through WebMCP.
All edits are staged and require approval.
Tool activity is recorded for technical users.
execution_rationale: Multiple frame sheets show coherent collection/onboarding and image-plus-text record states, with a clear approval concept, though exact end-to-end analytics are not legible.
execution_evidence: Seven gallery images and three frame sheets show collection/profile/onboarding-like surfaces.
Frames show populated image records with associated text and controls.
Live demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Collectors have a genuine burden of cataloging, valuation, and understanding what they own; the product addresses that niche directly.
impact_evidence: About text identifies manual entry of names, dates, purchase and current values as the problem.
Product supports nested boxes and useful analytics.
Frames show collection records and processing-like states.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent research and valuation to arbitrary collector niches with approval and auditability is a fresh angle on collection management.
creativity_evidence: Agent-automated onboarding handles niche product-line distinctions.
Staged review inbox and activity recording are integrated.
Concept connects external agent reasoning to local collection state.
usability_note: Approval inbox and nested collection model support safe use; the research/valuation experience is not fully observed.
red_flags: No transcript; exact valuation and analytics outcomes are not clearly readable in frames.
standouts: Good niche fit for agent-assisted data entry and research.
Safe staged-edit model.
advance_reason: Credible niche impact and a useful human-agent workflow merit advancement.

one_line: A WebMCP-native B-roll editor where agents propose and replan ghost edits while humans control the timeline.
what_it_does: RelayLab exposes transcript ranges, source moments, timeline positions, pacing opportunities, locks, and approval state so agents can plan visual-only B-roll overlays.
leverage_rationale: Agent access to semantic transcript/timeline state and human locks is materially more reliable than pixel-level editing automation, and replanning after human changes depends on shared structured state.
leverage_evidence: About text lists transcript ranges, source moments, timeline positions, ghost overlays, locks, and approval state as tools.
Agent cannot approve its own plan, change locks, or trigger paid generation.
Frame sheets show editor-like pages, previews, controls, and overlays.
execution_rationale: The stated collaboration loop is coherent and frames show a populated editing workspace, but the supplied stills do not clearly prove a proposal-to-replan-to-commit sequence.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo are reported alive.
Three sheets show video/editor workspaces with previews, controls, and media panels.
No transcript and no unambiguous final commit state.
impact_rationale: Creators can offload repetitive B-roll search and placement while preserving editorial judgment, a clear productivity and creative benefit.
impact_evidence: Product targets creators editing long talking-head videos.
About text describes search, proposal, human adjustment, replan, and approval loop.
Frames show media/editor surfaces.
creativity_rationale: Ghost edits plus agent replanning around human locks is a notably original collaboration model for video editing.
creativity_evidence: Keeps master audio/talking-head layer locked while agents work on visual overlays.
Human locks constrain replanning.
Agent proposes rather than autonomously commits creative edits.
usability_note: The ghost-edit and approval model preserves familiar editorial control; actual interaction quality needs observation.
red_flags: Frames do not clearly show an agent proposal, replan, or committed edited output.
standouts: Strong human-editor/agent collaboration boundary.
Semantic editing surface is a compelling WebMCP fit.
advance_reason: Distinctive creative workflow and strong leverage justify advancing to observe the actual editor loop.

leverage_rationale: Structured search across directories, events, and sponsorships is more reliable than scraping cards and forms, but the simulated site remains readily operable by general UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Five tools cover members, events, sponsorships, registration, and inquiries.
About text emphasizes structured results grounded in the same interface.

one_line: A file workspace where agents inspect context and prepare reviewable changes while humans control saves, approvals, restores, and access.
what_it_does: GoodFolder provides structured folders, files, document/table context, history, proposals, and comments through WebMCP, with durable human approval boundaries.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes semantic file/workspace state and reviewable proposals rather than brittle clicks, especially valuable for history-aware document and spreadsheet work.
leverage_evidence: About text lists folders, files, document structure, tables, history, and proposals as structured tools.
Agent can prepare proposals/comments but cannot silently save, approve, restore, remove, or alter access.
Frames show document/report states alongside technical panels and check indicators.
execution_rationale: The packet is coherent about seeded workspace, context/history, and approval constraints; frames show populated documents and apparent result states, though exact proposal approval flow is not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported alive.
Frames show populated document/report views, selected content, and apparent completion indicators.
Description provides a concrete seeded workflow with no signup/setup.
impact_rationale: Accountable agent work over real files addresses a broad and consequential need for context, auditability, correction, and human control.
impact_evidence: About text grounds the problem in understanding what happened after agents touch folders.
Supports Q3 report inspection, figure tracing, corrections, comments, and history.
Human makes final save/approval/access decisions.
creativity_rationale: Treating file history and reviewable proposals as the core human-agent collaboration surface is a strong original product framing.
creativity_evidence: History and reversibility are first-class rather than afterthoughts.
Visual judgment remains with the person while agent investigates/prepares.
WebMCP maps to semantic workspace concepts, not UI clicks.
usability_note: Seeded workspace and explicit forbidden mutations make the collaboration model understandable and safe.
red_flags: Exact approval and history-restore behavior are not fully legible in still frames.
standouts: Strong accountable-file-work concept.
Good safety boundary between preparation and mutation.
advance_reason: High practical impact and strong WebMCP fit with credible visible workspace evidence.

one_line: An open-data Berlin atlas where agents and people explore 542 neighbourhoods through shared map state and natural-language preferences.
what_it_does: navigator.berlin aggregates 65 open-data layers into neighbourhood scores and exposes map/filter state so an agent can translate conversational housing preferences into visual exploration.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes validated structured state behind a WebGL map, allowing agents to query and manipulate meaningful neighbourhood data that generic UI scraping cannot reliably access.
leverage_evidence: About text says the interesting state lives in a WebGL canvas and WebMCP exposes typed functions used by sliders.
65 layers and 542 areas are queryable with source/licence attached.
Packet describes shared agent/human slider state.
execution_rationale: The 175-second video transcript describes a coherent map, query, and collaboration workflow and the demo is reported alive; frame evidence is supportive but not fully legible for every result.
execution_evidence: Live demo, public repo, and 175-second video are reported.
About text specifies five-dimensional scoring, nine sliders, elections, and open-data layers.
Submitted sheets and screenshot show map, sliders, data, and tool-inspector surfaces.
impact_rationale: Residents choosing where to live have a real multi-criteria information problem, and aggregating fragmented civic datasets directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: About text identifies Berlin housing/neighbourhood decisions spanning a dozen datasets.
Product covers quietness, greenery, transit, culture, heat/noise, and elections.
Specific press/use claim and 542-area coverage support credible value.
creativity_rationale: Turning a conversational housing preference into shared, reversible map exploration over rich civic data is a notably original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent and human can move the same sliders and observe each other's actions.
Combines 65 datasets into live neighbourhood scoring.
Uses open-data provenance and licensing as part of answers.
usability_note: Conversational exploration layered onto familiar map sliders is promising, though density of civic data may challenge new users.
red_flags: Some claims rely on transcript/about text; exact visual details in frame sheets are small.
standouts: Excellent structured access to otherwise opaque WebGL state.
Strong civic-data and human-agent collaboration story.
advance_reason: Strong leverage, impact, and evidence-backed concept; advance.
